macro_events.title: Alphabet Q2 2026: Cloud +82%, Capex Raised to $195-205B, FCF Negative
macro_events.causal_chain: GOOGL reports $119.8B revenue (+24%), Cloud $24.8B (+82%), Cloud backlog $514B -> management raises full-year capex to $195-205B (from $180-190B) -> quarterly capex $44.9B exceeds operating cash flow -> FCF turns negative -$5.9B -> market worries about ROIC on AI investment -> GOOGL shares fall 3.8% after hours to $329 -> BUT capex flows to NVDA (GPUs), SK Hynix (HBM), Broadcom (custom ASICs) -> Asian chip stocks rally overnight (SK Hynix +6.5%, MediaTek +5.2%) -> net positive for semiconductor supply chain, net negative for Alphabet near-term equity value
macro_events.geographic_dimension: US-centric but supply chain benefits flow to South Korea (SK Hynix), Taiwan (TSMC, MediaTek), and Japan (Tokyo Electron)
macro_events.historical_analog: Meta Q3 2022: $9B capex guidance spooked market, stock fell 25% — but unlike Meta, Alphabet's Cloud has clear revenue acceleration (82% growth) to justify spend
macro_events.counterargument: Cloud backlog at $514B (+$50B QoQ) suggests revenue will catch up to capex within 2-3 quarters; negative FCF may be transient as Cloud margins expand

macro_events.title: Iran War Escalation: Houthi Bab al-Mandeb Blockade Opens Second Chokepoint
macro_events.causal_chain: US-Iran conflict ongoing since Feb 2026 -> Strait of Hormuz effectively closed (20% global oil, 20% LNG) -> IEA declared largest supply disruption in history -> now Houthis blockade Bab al-Mandeb strait -> this closes the Red Sea bypass route -> tankers must reroute via Cape of Good Hope (+12-14 days, +$2M/trip) -> war-risk insurance premiums spike on VLCCs -> WTI hits $88.17 (+1.54%), Brent $94.13 (+3.43%) -> Asian refiners face dual chokepoint closure -> European natgas (TTF) rises on Qatar LNG risk -> 10Y Treasury yields climb to 4.66% on inflation expectations -> Fed rate cut probability decreases -> equity multiples compress
macro_events.geographic_dimension: Middle East epicenter, global oil/LNG trade routes affected, Europe and Asia most exposed to energy supply disruption
macro_events.historical_analog: Sep 2019 Abqaiq attack — Brent +15% in 24h, tankers rallied 20-35% in one week; current disruption is structurally worse due to dual chokepoint closure
macro_events.counterargument: US Strategic Petroleum Reserve releases could cap upside; Saudi Arabia has spare capacity that could be activated; diplomatic breakthrough possible at any time

macro_events.geographic_dimension: US and China — Tesla's two largest markets, price war in China compressing margins
macro_events.historical_analog: Tesla Q2 2023 margin compression — stock fell 9% on similar margin squeeze, but recovered on robotaxi narrative; this time, operating margin is even lower at 1.4%
macro_events.counterargument: Record deliveries of 480K units show demand is intact; services segment hit record margins; FSD and Optimus robot could unlock non-auto revenue streams

macro_events.title: ECB Rate Decision: Expected Hold at 2.4% Amid Energy Shock Dilemma
macro_events.causal_chain: ECB hiked 25bp in June responding to Middle East energy shock -> Eurozone inflation re-accelerating on oil prices -> but growth is slowing (weak business activity, worsening labor market) -> ECB faces classic stagflation dilemma -> 95% probability of hold today -> hawkish rhetoric from Lagarde would strengthen EUR, weaken equities -> dovish surprise could spark risk-on rally
macro_events.geographic_dimension: Eurozone — indirect impact on US via EUR/USD and global risk appetite
macro_events.historical_analog: ECB July 2022 — first hike in 11 years amid similar inflation/growth dilemma
macro_events.counterargument: Market has 95% priced for hold — limited surprise potential; real volatility comes from Lagarde's press conference tone on September

affected_tickers.reason: German equities sensitive to ECB rate path

macro_events.title: China Section 301 Tariff Cliff: 10% Broad-Based Duty Expires July 24
macro_events.causal_chain: Section 301 10% broad tariff on Chinese goods set to expire July 24 -> Chinese exporters front-ran with 27% YoY export surge in June (strongest since Oct 2021) -> trade surplus hit $125.6B (near record) -> if tariff lapses: short-term deflationary for US importers -> if renewed/escalated: inflationary for retailers -> China GDP missed at 4.3% vs 4.5% target -> weak domestic demand means China remains export-dependent
macro_events.geographic_dimension: US-China bilateral — spillover to ASEAN manufacturing hubs and global supply chains
macro_events.historical_analog: May 2019 tariff escalation — S&P 500 fell 7% in three weeks on uncertainty
macro_events.counterargument: Even with expiration, existing Section 301 rates of 25-100% on many categories remain; net impact may be marginal
